comparison: Both evaluate GEPCOT cell identification and characterization (C3, C34-C38). OpenEval finds all claims C3, C34-C43 supported by converging evidence. Peer reviewers affirm data quality and support conclusions for the subset C3, C34-C38, stating data are 'extensive, of high quality' and support conclusions.

OpenEval R1 includes GEPCOT proliferation claims C39-C43, which peer R2 also evaluates as supported. Both agree BrdU incorporation data demonstrate GEPCOT proliferative activity as part of NIC characterization.

Both address short-lived nature of GEPCOT NICs. OpenEval R2 evaluates C4-C5, C44-C52 as supported by fate-mapping showing rapid turnover. Peer R3 evaluates overlapping claims C5, C44-C52 as supported, accepting the short-lived characterization without challenge.
Minor overlap on C4. OpenEval R2 includes C4 in comprehensive fate-mapping analysis. Peer R2 addresses C4 as part of proliferation findings, both finding it supported.

Both evaluate pre-GEPCOT quiescence characterization (C6-C9, C56, C58, C62-C64). OpenEval finds claims fully supported by low BrdU incorporation. Peer reviewers mark as UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about the relatively high 6% frequency being inconsistent with expectations for rare quiescent stem cells, requesting further discussion of heterogeneity.

Both evaluate pre-GEPCOT colony formation capacity (C10, C60-C61). OpenEval finds claims supported by extremely low neurosphere formation contrasting with GEPCOT cells. Peer reviewers mark as UNCERTAIN, noting cells must proliferate under some conditions since they repopulate GEPCOTs after ablation, requesting data on growth factor requirements.

Both evaluate pre-GEPCOT as long-lived stem cells (C11-C15, C53-C54, C68-C71). OpenEval finds claims supported by sustained labeling over 60 days with multiple Cre lines. Peer reviewers agree, stating findings 'make a significant contribution' to identifying the 'true' quiescent adult neural stem cell.

Both evaluate evidence against dedifferentiation (C65-C67). OpenEval finds claims supported by lack of pre-GEPCOT labeling by NIC markers. Peer reviewers agree, accepting this as evidence for unidirectional hierarchy from qNSCs to NICs.

Both evaluate lineage progression from pre-GEPCOT to downstream populations (C72-C77). OpenEval finds claims supported by temporal fate-mapping with rigorous quantification. Peer reviewers agree, accepting this as part of high-quality dataset supporting hierarchical model.

Both evaluate morphological characterization (C78-C81). OpenEval finds claims supported by whole-mount immunostaining consistent with prior literature. Peer reviewers agree, not questioning the morphological data.

Both evaluate TMZ ablation and regeneration experiments (C16-C18, C82-C92). OpenEval finds all claims supported by differential TMZ sensitivity and lineage tracing. Peer reviewers agree on overlapping claims C16-C18, C82-C85, C87-C92, accepting this as strong evidence for hierarchical relationship. Minor difference: OpenEval includes C86 which peer review doesn't explicitly address.

Both evaluate constitutive Bmi-1 deletion phenotypes (C19-C20, C93, C101, C108-C113). OpenEval finds comprehensive evidence supported across multiple readouts. Peer reviewers agree on this subset, accepting progressive depletion as demonstrating Bmi-1's role in NSC maintenance.

OpenEval R10 includes claims C94-C100 about GFAP staining and cell frequency changes. Peer R16 marks these as UNCERTAIN, requesting to see the enhanced GFAP staining data rather than just allusion to it, indicating incomplete presentation.
OpenEval R10 includes neurosphere functional deficits (C105-C107). Peer R18 evaluates these separately as supported, accepting data demonstrating Bmi-1's requirement for NSC function in culture.

Both evaluate differential Cdkn2a expression (C115-C119, with peer also including C21). OpenEval finds claims supported by qRT-PCR data. Peer reviewers mark as UNCERTAIN, asking whether senescence is the relevant mechanism for cell depletion, indicating mechanistic link requires further investigation.

Both evaluate inducible Bmi-1 deletion effects (C120-C140 for OpenEval, C132-C140 for peer). OpenEval finds comprehensive temporal analysis supported across multiple readouts. Peer reviewers agree on C132-C140, accepting progressive depletion and loss of neurosphere function.

OpenEval R12 includes neurogenesis decline claims (C103-C104, C121-C125). Peer R12 evaluates C103-C104, C121-C125 as supported, accepting progressive neurogenesis decline as consistent with stem cell depletion.

OpenEval R12 includes gliogenesis claims (C126-C127). Peer R13 evaluates these as supported but notes proportions of new glia seem very small and requests comparison of relative proportions—a request for additional analysis rather than challenge to data.

OpenEval R12 includes proliferation decline claims (C129-C131). Peer R19 evaluates these as supported, accepting progressive decline in proliferating populations as consistent with stem cell depletion.

Both evaluate differential timing of pre-GEPCOT versus GEPCOT depletion (C141-C148). OpenEval finds claims supported though notes lack of statistical significance for pre-GEPCOT depletion at 12 months. Peer reviewers mark as UNCERTAIN, asking about senescence mechanisms, indicating functional consequences of p16 expression require further investigation.
OpenEval R14 evaluates background claims C1-C2 about prior field knowledge as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found—these are contextual rather than novel findings.

OpenEval R15 evaluates established background knowledge claims C22-C30 as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found—these provide context but are not novel findings requiring peer assessment.
OpenEval R16 evaluates methodological baseline claims C31-C33 as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found—these are methodological details rather than major findings.

OpenEval R17 evaluates pre-GEPCOT heterogeneity claim C59 as supported by antibody staining. No corresponding peer review evaluation found—this is a descriptive finding supporting population characterization.
OpenEval R18 evaluates control observations C55, C57 as supported. Peer R4 includes C57 in broader pre-GEPCOT characterization marked as UNCERTAIN due to concerns about population frequency.
OpenEval R19 evaluates established mechanistic knowledge C114 about Bmi-1 and Cdkn2a as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found—this is background context from prior literature.

OpenEval R20 evaluates overall significance claim C149 as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found—this represents broader significance rather than specific experimental result requiring peer assessment.
